newsitem.title: POLAND: Polifarb W eyes Cieszyn merger at mid '97.
newsitem.headline: Polifarb W eyes Cieszyn merger at mid '97.

text.p: The planned merger between Polifarb Wroclaw and Polifarb Cieszyn, the first friendly takeover in Warsaw bourse history, could be completed by July 1997, a Wroclaw deputy president said.

"If everything goes smoothly the merger could take place at the end of the first half," Wladyslaw Burczak told Reuters on Friday, adding that shareholder meetings approving the decision could be held by the end of the first quarter.
Burczak said Cieszyn, which along with Wroclaw announced on Thursday it sought the merger, had to raise its share capital by 2,978,820 shares to equal Wroclaw's 22,103,820 shares.
"There's no threat for the stockholders of either side," Burczak said.
Later Cieszyn would set another issue for Wroclaw shareholders and a one-for-one share exhange would take place to effect the merger, Burczak said.
He said that because both companies were similar in size and market capitalisation shareholders of neither firm would lose out on the deal.
Burczak said the new entity would be able to produce at both Wroclaw and Cieszyn, wherever each centre produced a given product more efficiently.
He said the city of Wroclaw was chosen as the headquarters of the new firm because of its proximity to Berlin and Prague and its industrial and scientific heritage.
Burczak said Dutch Akzo-Nobel as well as several German and Austrian firms provided tough competition to the Polifarbs, which analysts said would now be better positioned against foreign producers.
"They (the Polifarbs) were big in their own pond but certainly midgets when it came to the real scale of things, so that's a very good step forward," said Stephen Pettyfer of Merrill Lynch in London.
Over the first 11 months this year Polifarb Cieszyn made a net profit of 20 million zlotys on sales of 289.4 million zlotys. Wroclaw netted 19.5 million on sales of 196 million.
Both stocks surged on Friday by nearly the daily 10 percent limit on the back of the merger news and analysts said the plan could underpin their prices for some time.
